## Analysis

**Reading the logs (task_score ≈ forward speed in m/s):**

| Cand | iter 500 task_score | recent trend (last 200 it) | key structural property |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | **7.45** (max 8.10) | +1.6, noisy but climbing | tanh temp 10 (nearly linear at 7 m/s) **+ linear high-speed bonus above 5 m/s** |
| C2 | 6.38 | +1.0, decelerating | tanh(3) fully saturated; Gaussian tracking hump **caps the optimum at ~9.5 m/s** |
| C3 | 5.25 | +1.6, steady, non-decelerating | **linear** in vx (gated by uprightness), no saturation, no meaningful penalties |
| C4 | 5.98 | +1.1, decelerating | tanh(6) saturating + linear clipped at 15 m/s, several regularizers |

**Why C1 wins:**
- It starts from a clear lead (7.45 vs 6.38/5.98/5.25) and its *shaping gradient is still healthy at its current speed*: d/dv[tanh(v/10)] ≈ 0.06/m/s plus the high-speed bonus ≈ 0.033/m/s, i.e. roughly linear, so there is no plateau to fall into.
- Its penalty terms are deliberately tiny (control 0.005, lateral 0.02, joint-limit soft 0.05), so they don't brake an aggressive gait; the tilt penalty fires only below up_z = 0.4, so it blocks tumbling exploits without capping speed.
- The high-speed bonus is already active (0.09 at iter 500) and grows linearly to 14 m/s, giving a persistent push that the other candidates lack in the 6–10 m/s band.

**Why C3 is the runner-up:** its reward is essentially the metric itself (gated_forward_speed ≈ task_score in the log), the gradient never flattens (no tanh, no tracking hump that switches sign past its target), and its regularizers are negligible — so it has the highest asymptotic ceiling and the most consistent improvement rate (+0.4 / 50 it, not decaying). It only trails because it started 2.2 m/s behind; the remaining 2,500 iterations are enough to close that gap.

**C2 third:** it starts ahead of C4 but its dominant term is a Gaussian tracking bump peaking at 9 m/s — the policy is actively *rewarded for stopping there* (gradient → 0 and then negative above 9). Its lateral-drift penalty is also growing (-0.33), further damping speed.

**C4 last:** weakest combination — a saturating tanh(6) plus a clipped linear term, plus the largest control/lateral/angular regularizer set; it shows the clearest deceleration (last 100 it: +0.29) and no mechanism to keep pushing at high speed.

**Projection at 3,000 iters:** C1 ≈ 10–12 m/s, C3 ≈ 9–12 m/s, C2 ≈ 9–10 m/s (capped), C4 ≈ 8–10 m/s.
